intro: Real plans and imagined situations use different forms of si.
b1.titulo: A real plan or an imagined one?
b1.texto:
For a real or possible condition, use **si + present**. The result can be in the present, future or imperative: **Si tengo tiempo, voy / iré / te llamo**.

For an imagined or unlikely situation, use **si + imperfect subjunctive**, then the **conditional**: **Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría más**. The situation is imagined; the speaker does not say it is impossible.

The imperfect subjunctive often comes from the third-person plural past: **tuvieron → tuviera**, **hicieron → hiciera**, **fueron → fuera**. Its endings are **-ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran**; remember the written accent in **habláramos**.

Do not put the conditional after **si** in these patterns: **Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría** (not *si tendría*).
b2.nota: The second pattern can refer to an unreal present or an unlikely future.
b3.f0: If I could leave work for a year, I would travel around South America.
b3.f1: And what would you do with the flat?
b3.f2: If I rented it out, I would have money for the trip.
b3.f3: If I were in your place, I would talk it through calmly.
b4.f0: Marta has been thinking about taking a long trip for years, but she never finds the right time.
b4.f1: If she had six months free, she would visit several countries by train.
b4.f2: She would also learn some Portuguese before leaving and look for accommodation in advance.
b4.f3: Her brother asks what she would do about her job.
b4.f4: Marta replies that if she could work remotely, she would not have to leave it.
b4.f5: For now she only has two weeks of holiday, so she is planning a shorter route.
b6.pregunta: What would Marta do if she had six months free?
b6.o0.refuerzo: She would travel by train through several countries.
b6.o1.refuerzo: She is considering options, not saying she would leave it.
b7.pregunta: Why is Marta planning a shorter route now?
b7.o0.refuerzo: The final sentence gives her current situation.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The train is part of her imagined plan.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The text does not say this.
b8.pregunta: Which sentence best sums up the text?
b8.o0.refuerzo: This combines her imagined plan and her current situation.
b8.o1.refuerzo: The text describes an idea, not a completed move.
b8.o2.refuerzo: She would like to travel by train.
b9.pregunta: Complete the imagined situation: if I had time, I would travel.
b9.o0.refuerzo: Imperfect subjunctive after si; conditional in the result.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The conditional does not go in this si clause.
b9.o2.refuerzo: This would describe a real or possible condition.
b10.traduccion: If I could work remotely, I would not leave my job.
